statement: A happy prefix of a string is a non-empty prefix that is also a suffix, but is not the whole string.
You are given a string s of lowercase letters. Return its longest happy prefix, or an empty string if it has none.
The length of the answer is the last entry of the KMP LPS array of s.

examples.explanation: "abab" opens the string and also closes it. No longer prefix appears at the end, so the answer is "abab".
"aab" is both the first and the last three characters; "aaba" and longer prefixes do not end the string.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
